Make Your High Score Stick! — NVS

Use permanent memory so the best score survives power-off

What we're doing: You've built a working quiz — awesome! But there's one problem: when you turn the Tab5 off, the high score disappears. We can fix this with something called NVS (Non-Volatile Storage). It's a special memory that survives power-offs!

🧩 Analogy Regular variables are like writing on a whiteboard — erase the power and it's gone. NVS is like carving your score into stone — it stays there until you deliberately change it.
📝 The Two Halves of NVS NVS needs two things to work: reading the saved score when the program starts (we'll do this now), and saving a new high score when someone beats it (you already added this in Step 5 inside show_gameover!). Together they make your high score last forever.

A) Load the Saved High Score on Startup

  1. Open System → NVS in the toolbox
  2. In Setup, find your set high_score to 0 block
  3. Drag nvs get integer "high_score" into Setup
  4. Replace the 0 in set high_score to 0 with the nvs get integer "high_score" block

Your Setup now reads:

set high_score to nvs get integer "high_score"
💡 Magic! The first time you run the program, no high score exists yet. nvs.getInt is smart — when a key doesn't exist, it just returns 0. So the high score starts at 0 and only goes up from there!

B) You Already Set Up the Saving Part!

Remember the nvs set integer "high_score" high_score block you added inside show_gameover() back in Step 5? That's the other half of NVS — it saves the high score when someone beats it.

Here's how the two halves work together:

🔍 The NVS Cycle:
1️⃣ On startup: nvs get integer "high_score" reads the saved score (or returns 0 if none)
2️⃣ During play: high_score lives in a regular variable — fast to read and change
3️⃣ When beaten: nvs set integer "high_score" high_score carves the new best into stone
4️⃣ Next startup: The saved score is read again — it's still there!

C) Test It!

  1. Run your program, play a full game, and beat your own high score
  2. Turn the Tab5 off and on again
  3. Run the program again — the best score is still there! 🎉
✅ What you should see: After restarting the Tab5, your best_score_label shows the saved high score instead of 0/8. It survived the power-off — you carved it into stone!
💾 Final checkpoint! 🎉 You did it! You built a complete picture quiz game with three screens, scoring, high score tracking, AND permanent storage. Your high score now lives forever — just like a real arcade game!

You're Done! Here's What You Built

A complete recap of your amazing quiz game

Let's trace through your entire program one more time:

  1. Setup: The Tab5 wakes up, screen turns on, score = 0, current_round = 1, high_score = loaded from NVS. Title screen appears.
  2. START tapped: Score resets to 0, round resets to 1. setup_round() loads the first picture and fills buttons. Game screen appears.
  3. Answer tapped: Button calls check_answer(1, 2, 3, or 4). Function compares to correct_index[current_round]. If match → score +1. Round advances. More rounds? → setup_round(). All done? → show_gameover().
  4. Game over: Final score displays. If you beat the high score, it's saved to NVS — forever! Game-over screen appears.
  5. Try Again: Back to the title screen. The high score is still there, waiting to be beaten.
  6. Loop: M5.update() runs over and over, keeping the touch screen responsive.
🧠 What You Learned Variables (jars for numbers) • Lists (numbered shelves) • Lists of lists (bookshelves) • Events (doorbell responders) • If/else (decision makers) • Functions (reusable recipes) • Page navigation (flipping book pages) • NVS (carving into stone). That's 8 powerful concepts — and you used them all in one program!
